reasoning.text: The horse left the hollow alone and nobody led it away; Brown only found it loose afterwards. Straker was cutting at the horse by match-light, as the knife, candle, vesta and lamed sheep suggest, so the horse itself most likely struck the blow.
Derbyshire's letters come to Straker's house, his bill was in Straker's pocket, and Mrs. Straker never had the costly dress. The 'friend' is very likely Straker under another name.

The dog made no noise, so whoever came to the stable that night was someone it knew. The door was locked at nine and open at seven; Straker had a key, went out alone at one, and died beside the horse.
The silent dog points to Straker as the man who took the horse, and he needed the lad asleep. Only Hunter's portion of the curry from Straker's own house held opium.
The police arrested Simpson as the natural suspect: a gentleman bookmaker lodging half a mile off with bets against the favourite, which fits the gentlemanly stranger asking for a tip.
Straker carried a cataract knife for fine cuts, uncorked it and struck a light in the hollow beside the horse, and the paddock sheep have gone lame as if from practice.
An uncorked cataract knife, a candle and a struck match in the hollow by the horse, and lamed sheep: the knife was for a delicate cut on the horse.
The cutting needed a light, free arms and privacy, away from the lad and the lads in the loft.
Straker's knife was meant for a subcutaneous nick to the horse's tendon, and the lamed sheep are in the paddock by his own villa, so he practised the cut on them.
On a still night the coat was laid across the bush, not torn off or blown there; the cork guard lay by the body. He took the coat off to have his arms free for some work.
If Straker led the horse out alone past a dog that knew him, Simpson was never in the hollow, so the cravat Simpson says he lost was picked up by Straker himself.

Brown, an old horse-faker, asked whether to 'change it' first and Holmes told him not to; Holmes asked whether Ross would know his horse. The blaze and leg could be dyed, so the plain bay in Ross's colours is Silver Blaze.
The household ate the same dish unharmed, so the opium went into Hunter's portion only, after his share was set apart.
